readme.overview: The module addresses two operational concerns: - **Who changed what, and when** — by subscribing to domain events and persisting structured, field-level diffs for tracked entities (with deep child-record nesting). - **What did the system actually send and receive over HTTP** — by attaching request/response bodies and headers to Application Insights telemetry for both inbound requests and outbound dependencies, based on configurable rules. Both features are designed to be non-intrusive: change tracking runs on a background channel so domain handlers return immediately, and telemetry enrichment falls back gracefully when the settings cache is cold.
keyFeatures: Subscribes to `GenericChangedEntryEvent<T>` and compares old/new snapshots.
Tracks **primitive collections** (e.g. `IList<string> Tags`) via set equality.
Tracks **ValueObject child collections** matched by position.
Supports **deep nesting** — child records can carry their own child records (e.g. Contact → Organization → Address).
Each record stores operation type (`Added` / `Modified` / `Deleted`), changed fields with old/new values, and a tree of child records.
Domain events are processed **asynchronously** through a bounded `Channel<T>` and a background `IHostedService`, so event publishers are not blocked.
**`HttpLoggingMiddleware`** captures inbound request/response content for matching routes.
**`HttpTelemetryInitializer`** enriches outgoing `DependencyTelemetry` (Application Insights) with request/response content and headers.
Per-host / per-method / per-path rules with independent limits for request and response body length.
Settings are kept in a singleton in-memory cache, pre-warmed at startup and invalidated automatically when the management API mutates them.
Cold-cache reads on the telemetry path are bounded by a short timeout so a slow database never blocks the request pipeline.
